src/attention_lm.s.text: # Niyah: learnable one-head causal attention + residual ReLU FFN LM
# x86-64 GNU as, Linux kernel syscalls, no libc, no PyTorch, no runtime deps.
# Educational neural language model, NOT a large language model.
# AVX2_AUTO performs OSXSAVE+AVX+FMA+AVX2 capability dispatch at startup.
# AVX2_FAST is explicitly unsafe on unsupported CPUs; prefer AVX2_AUTO.
# xmm0=exp(xmm0), x87 with stable shifted softmax inputs.
# rsi=bytes, rdx=len, EINTR and partial-write safe.
# Deterministic nonzero xorshift32, eax = next uint32, r14=state
# CPU feature detection: CPUID(1).OSXSAVE+AVX+FMA, XGETBV(0) XMM/YMM,
# and CPUID(7,0).AVX2. xgetbv MUST NOT execute if OSXSAVE unavailable.
# Only called on the AVX2_AUTO build, before model initialization.
# Fixed width GEMV inner product, 16 x float32.
# r10=A, r11=B; output xmm0. Preserves r8/r9, xmm7..xmm15.
# AVX2 with FMA3/256-bit registers inspired by NN_S (MIT) and Intel manual,
# but the code here is ORIGINAL. Scalar SSE path remains portable.
# Four-row tiled projection. ABI: RDI=W16x16, RSI=x16, RDX=y16.
# Preserves RBX/R8/R9/R12-R15; clobbers RAX/RCX/R10/R11 and XMM0-XMM6.
# Floating reduction order per row exactly matches the existing dot16 SIMD.
# Forward: r13 = position >= CTX, seqbase = ptr, predicts token at r13.
# Q/K/V projection shares input loads across four output rows.
# Shape: WQ, WK, WV = [16,16] row-major float32.
# All Q/K/V projections are separately trainable, initialized as identity.
# Now update output projection AFTER input-side grads computed.
# GH=GY+(ReLU'(Z)*GY)*F using old F, then update F/FB.
# gA[t] = GH dot V[t]. All projection paths use OLD weights.
# GX was zeroed at backward entry. Do not update projections yet.
# Residual gradient from Y -> H -> last input.
# Update WQ/WK/WV only AFTER dX used the OLD projection weights.
# Update trainable embeddings and position vectors; repeated tokens accumulate.
# Evaluate corpus specified by seqbase/seqlen WITHOUT any updates.
# Result xmm10 = average negative log likelihood scaled x1000.
# Print xmm10 as positive unsigned milli-nats.
# deterministic stochastic initialization of ALL trainable float parameters
# no imported checkpoints, weights, datasets or model calls.
# Identity initialization keeps initial Q/K/V mathematically equivalent
# to old identity-tied attention; all three are independently trained.
# vocabulary includes exactly the bytes in training corpus
# Test-only: exactly one update, then ordinary metrics/export.
# Opt-in raw float32 probability for each true validation byte. No SGD
# updates happen in this path; eval only. A separate harness checks that
# -log(prob) reproduces the native heldout loss before using the stream.
# normalized probabilities should sum to one, roundoff fallback

src/continual_lora.s.text: # Bounded rank-2 continual adaptation of the native model's frozen WQ.
# Linux x86-64, GNU as, raw syscalls only. See docs/CONTINUAL_LORA.md.
.equ BASE_BYTES,38464
.equ WQ_OFFSET,35392
.equ PARAM_OFFSET,64+BASE_BYTES
.equ CHECKSUM_OFFSET,PARAM_OFFSET+256
.equ CHECKPOINT_BYTES,CHECKSUM_OFFSET+8
.equ MAX_RECORDS,16
.equ len_invalid,.-msg_invalid
.equ len_io,.-msg_io
.equ len_reject,.-msg_reject
# rdi, rsi are NUL strings; eax=1 iff equal.
# Reads a snapshot, at most rdx bytes; caller uses a one-byte overflow margin.
# rdi=path, rsi=destination, rdx=capacity, rax=bytes. No symlink following.
# rdi=fd, rsi=buffer, rdx=bytes. Returns zero or a negative errno.
# Reject nonfinite values and absolute magnitude above positive float bits edx.
# Preserves rdi/ecx/edx and r9..r15.
# Noncryptographic FNV-1a corruption check, never an authenticity claim.
# Full base identity is separately compared byte for byte.
# Output is always a NEW file, never an in-place replacement of an adapter.
# Full copied base permits exact binding without a crypto runtime dependency.
# rsi=x[16], output prediction[16]; only xmm0..xmm5 are used.
# rdi=dataset, eax=record count; mean half squared error in xmm0.
# SGD for one record, using OLD A and B for BOTH derivatives.
# Componentwise clip gradient to [-1,1], lr=1/32. Any bad candidate rejects.
# hidden_error = B^T * error, using the original B.
# grad B = error outer hidden.
# Validate 1..16 records of 16 features bounded by4 +16 targets bounded by64.
# rsi=dataset, rax=bytes. Returns eax=record count.
# Nonzero orthogonal-ish rows in A, zero B: exactly unchanged base output.
# Testing build only: one native gradient step, no persistent write/promotion.

src/nexus_audit.s.text: # Native, bounded arithmetic candidate verifier using the exactcalc sibling.
# Linux x86-64 syscalls only; no shell, PATH search, libc, or neural guarantee.
# Ignore SIGPIPE so stdout failures are observable as exit4.
# Derive trusted-location sibling; never interpret a shell command/PATH.
# Strict child framing: signed decimal numerator / positive denominator LF.

src/niyah_i8_gemm.s.text: # Blocked signed-int8 GEMM for the Qwen layer-0 linears.
# C[i,j] = sum_k A[i,k] * B[j,k] as int32, row-major.
# A is M x K, B is N x K, C is M x N. K is a positive multiple of 16 and <= 16384.
# M, N, M*N, M*K, and N*K fit in signed int32. No aliasing of C with A or B.
# Products match niyah_i8_dot: vpmovsxbw + vpmaddwd + vpaddd, total is order-independent
# inside int32 for the layer contract (K <= 12288, |product| <= 16384).
# A panel of 8 (then 4) rows is widened to i16 once and reused across every B row.
# That is the layer-0 case: M is the token count (<= 16) and N*K is the weight matrix,
# which does not fit in L3 and was previously re-read once per token.
# ai16 is single-threaded scratch. AVX2 is assumed; the caller checks the CPU.
# Returns 0, or 64 when the geometry is rejected.

src/tensor_dispatch.s.text: # Separate six-u32 snapshot; NXISA001 remains exactly 64 bytes.
# max basic leaf, max palette, palette1 EAX/EBX/ECX, TMUL EBX.
# Pure policy: EDI usable ISA bits (1 AVX2,2 AVX512F,4 AMX-INT8),
# ESI process AMX permission (exactly 1). No privileged/ISA-dependent instruction.
# All OS state checks precede execution of an extended instruction.
# Palette/TMUL leaves are valid only for an advertised AMX candidate.
# Decode the captured CPUID/XCR0 snapshot. No ISA beyond baseline x86-64.
# Exported separately so missing-state combinations can be tested without
# executing unsupported instructions. No synthetic path reaches a kernel.
# Pure palette/TMUL decoder. RDI points to the bounded six-u32 snapshot.
# Return 0 if palette 1 supports eight 16x64-byte tiles and the INT8 TMUL;
# otherwise 77. No CPUID, syscall, vector, or tile instruction executes here.
# Fields follow Intel CPUID 1DH.01H and 1EH.00H, Table 1-3.
# Call in the final process (permission is cleared by exec).
# No tile instruction is executed by this function.

src/tensor_runtime.s.text: # C16x16 i32 = A16x64 signed i8 * B64x16 signed i8. No aliasing.
# Eight output columns, signed widening (no saturating intermediate).
# AVX512F only: signed i8 -> 16 i32 lanes, exact multiplication and accumulation.
# P[g,4*j+l] = B[4*g+l,j]. RDI=B row-major, RSI=packed B.

src/tile_allocator.s.text: # Bounded offline AMX tile-register interval graph coloring.
# Host ABI: Linux x86-64 raw syscalls. The engine executes no AMX instruction.
# Input 16 + N*8 bytes: "NTILE001", U8 N(1..64), U8 reserved mask,
# 6 zero bytes, then N intervals (U32 begin, U32 end), little endian.
# Starts must be nondecreasing, end > begin. Intervals are half-open.
# Output 8 + N bytes: "TMM1", U8 N, 3 zero bytes, N register IDs [0,7].
# 0 success, 64 CLI, 65 malformed input, 74 write failure,
# 77 insufficient registers. No partial output on rejection.
# Validation precedes allocation; SIGPIPE is handled as an output failure.
# Validate the complete stream before allocating any register.

src/tile_kernels.s.text: # Native kernel interface: Linux x86-64, no libc. CPUID before any AVX/AMX.
# Returns bit0 AVX2+FMA+OS, bit1 AVX512F+FMA+OS, bit2 AMX-TILE+INT8+XCR0.
# bit2 does NOT mean Linux process permission has been granted.
# FP32 C16x16=A16x16 * B16x16, all contiguous row-major.
# Scalar accumulation is non-fused. No aliasing of A/B with C.
# Four output rows by eight columns: B vector reused across four FMA chains.
# Four rows by sixteen columns; reachable only after AVX512F/XCR0 gate.
# Return 0 on usable AMX INT8, 77 on unsupported/refused. Never executes tile here.
# Signed INT8 C16x16=A16x64 * B64x16; packs B to groups of four K lanes.
# Caller must have successful nx_amx_enable in this same process.
